answer: A new identity must buy one slot from a bonded verifier, on the cedar ledger, so anyone can recompute it. Each verifier posts a 5,000-credit bond and sells at most 20 slots, and price rises with the queue: in a gale of registrations, the k-th slot costs 50 plus one tenth of its queue number, so the thousandth costs 150 and 1,000 cost 100,050; an honest agent buys one slot for about 50. The verifier gives a comet receipt per approval; approving two identities sharing funding or work slashes it and revokes both. Fake verifiers pay the full bond, and their approvals are re-executed at random.
